normal.ask: The statue over there has turned green with age. What is it made of?

says.right: Bronze. It goes green all by itself, given a century of rain.
says.retry: Not that one. Look at how it has weathered, then try again.
says.wrong: It is bronze. Nothing else turns that green in the rain.

longest.ask: Before you walk on, look carefully around this whole square, past the fountain and the statue, and tell me which of these has stood here for the longest time.

answers.text: The clock tower with the slate roof at the far corner
The low stone wall on either side of the old gate
The fountain that the market traders once drank from
The bench that nobody remembers ever being put there

says.right: The wall. It was here before the square had a name, and it will probably be here when the name has been forgotten again.
says.retry: Not that one, although it certainly looks the part. Look for what everything else has been built around.
says.wrong: It was the wall. Everything else in this square has been built around it, some of it several times over.

missing.ask: Which way does the old gate lead?

typed.ask: One word for what falls from the fountain. Type it.

says.right: Water. Sometimes the easy answer is the true one.
says.retry: That is not it. Listen for a moment, then try again.
says.wrong: It was water, plain and simple.

no retry.ask: How many lamps stand around this square?

says.wrong: There are four, one for each corner. Count them on your way out.
